edges.label: the second named channel, under SECDEF and USD(I&S) rather than the DNI
edges.note: The Military Intelligence Program is the defence-side counterpart to the NIP, managed by the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. DoD has disclosed a MIP appropriated topline annually since 2010 and request figures since 2012; the DoD Financial Management Regulation Vol. 2B Ch. 16 governs how intelligence programmes are budgeted and displayed. Topline-only disclosure is the same structural property as the NIP.

a.label: Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence

edges.label: the OSD element with policy authority over intelligence, counterintelligence, security and sensitive activities
edges.note: OUSD(I), since 2020 OUSD(I&S), is where the sensitive-activities policy authority sits and where the whole Elizondo/AATIP dispute takes place. It is also the office under which the Military Intelligence Program is managed, which makes it the point where this domain's organisational and funding threads meet.

title: DoD Financial Management Regulation, Volume 2B, Chapter 16, 'Intelligence Programs/Activities'
